title: Accounts Assistant
description:
As an Accounts Assistant, you will support the day-to-day financial operations of a retail business, processing transactions, maintaining accurate records, and assisting with budgeting, reconciliations, and financial reporting. Working closely with finance, marketing, and external partners, you will help ensure costs are recorded correctly, resolve account queries, and provide reliable administrative support to keep the finance function running smoothly.

Client Details
- Established international organisation
- Operates in the retail industry
- Located in Reading

Description

Accounts Assistant responsibilities:
- Maintain accurate financial records, ensuring all accounting information, cost entries, and supporting documentation are up to date and well organised
- Process day-to-day finance administration, including the creation and maintenance of budgets, posting financial transactions, and updating records within finance systems
- Monitor and track spend against budgets, working closely with internal stakeholders to ensure financial data is recorded accurately and reported effectively
- Generate and process customer credit notes, cost recharges, and other financial adjustments in line with agreed procedures and deadlines
- Analyse financial data to identify discrepancies, investigate variances, and support the resolution of account, vendor, and customer queries
- Assist with month-end activities, reconciliations, reporting, and ensuring income and expenditure are accurately accounted for
- Support promotional and commercial activities by maintaining relevant financial records, monitoring spend, and ensuring compliance with internal processes
- Collaborate with colleagues across finance and wider business functions to ensure tasks are completed accurately, efficiently, and within required timescales
- Provide clear and professional support to internal and external stakeholders, responding to finance-related queries and helping to maintain strong working relationships

Profile

A successful Accounts Assistant should have:
- Previous experience in an Accounts Assistant, Finance Assistant, or similar finance administration role, with a strong understanding of day-to-day accounting processes
- Confident maintaining accurate financial records, processing transactions, and handling sensitive financial information with a high level of attention to detail
- Strong analytical skills with the ability to review financial data, identify discrepancies, investigate variances, and resolve issues efficiently
- Microsoft Excel skills, including the use of Pivot Tables, VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, reconciliations, and data analysis
- Experience using finance systems such as SAP or similar ERP systems
- Excellent organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and maintain accuracy
- Strong communication and stakeholder management skills
- Proactive and self-motivated, able to work independently while contributing effectively as part of a collaborative team
- A solid understanding of core accounting principles, including budgeting, reconciliations, financial reporting, and month-end processes

Job Offer

Accounts Assistant:
- Salary: £34,000 to £37,000 per annum - dependent on experience
- Competitive benefits package (TBC)
- Reading location, well-connected by public transport
- Hybrid working
- A supportive and inclusive workplace culture

title: Accounts Assistant
description:
Accounts Assistant - Maidenhead - £28,000 / £31,000

About the Client

Wade Macdonald are currently working with a well-established organisation with a presence across London, seeking an Accounts Assistant to join their finance team in Maidenhead. The organisation offers a welcoming and collaborative working environment, where teamwork, accuracy and strong professional relationships are highly valued. With a supportive culture and a commitment to employee development, this is an excellent opportunity to build your finance career.

About the Job

This is a fantastic opportunity for an Accounts Assistant to join a busy, medium-sized finance team. The role offers a varied workload, providing hands-on experience across different areas of accounting while working closely with experienced finance professionals.

Duties will include:
- Obtaining banking records and ensuring financial transactions are accurately recorded.
- Completing bank and supplier account reconciliations, investigating and resolving discrepancies.
- Assisting with the production of financial reports and maintaining accurate accounting records.
- Monitoring incoming and outgoing transactions, including credit and debit balances.
- Processing BACS payments and supporting payment administration.
- Providing general accounting assistance and undertaking additional tasks across the wider finance department.

About the Successful Applicant

The successful candidate will have 1 - 2 years of experience in a finance or accounts-related position, with a good understanding of basic accounting processes and reconciliations. You will be organised, detail-oriented and confident working with financial information. Strong communication skills, a proactive approach and a willingness to learn are essential, alongside the ability to work effectively as part of a team.

What You Will Receive in Return

You will join a friendly and supportive finance team where you can develop your accounting knowledge and gain valuable exposure to a wide range of finance activities. Working alongside experienced colleagues, you will benefit from practical guidance, opportunities to broaden your responsibilities and a collaborative environment that encourages professional growth. Parking is also available, making this an excellent opportunity to establish a strong foundation for your future finance career.

title: Accounts Receivable Assistant
description:
Morgan McKinley are a growing international business to recruit an Accounts Receivable & Billing Assistant on a fixed-term contract.

This is a hands-on opportunity for someone with experience in billing, accounts receivable or credit control to take ownership of the end-to-end billing and collections process across multiple entities and currencies.

Key Responsibilities:
- Prepare and issue accurate client invoices, ensuring billing schedules are up to date.
- Manage aged debt, proactively chasing outstanding payments by phone and email.
- Allocate incoming receipts, including multi-currency payments, and reconcile the sales ledger.
- Resolve billing queries and liaise with internal stakeholders and clients.
- Produce aged debt and cash collection reports.
- Support month-end reconciliations and identify opportunities to improve processes.

About you:
- 2+ years' experience in billing, accounts receivable or credit control.
- Available on immediate notice, to start at short notice
- Background in a service-based business such as professional services, recruitment, consultancy, legal or SaaS.
- Strong communication skills and confidence dealing with senior client contacts.
- Excellent attention to detail and good Excel skills, including lookups and pivot tables.
- Experience with Xero and multi-currency invoicing is advantageous but not essential.

title: Accounts Receivable Clerk
description:
Orka Financial is recruiting an Accounts Receivable Clerk for a temporary assignment in Reading through to 26 February 2027. This full-time, 35-hour role pays £16-£18 per hour and offers hybrid working, with three days in the office and two from home. Parking is available on site.

The opportunity

Reporting into the Financial Controller, you will take ownership of day-to-day receivables and treasury activity across UK and international operations. You will help keep customer accounts accurate, cash properly allocated and records ready for year-end and external audit.

What you will be doing
- Preparing and posting sales invoices with the correct customer, currency and tax treatment.
- Allocating receipts, investigating unallocated cash and keeping the debtors ledger reconciled.
- Chasing overdue balances and resolving invoice queries with customers and internal teams.
- Completing cashbooks and bank reconciliations across multiple accounts and currencies.
- Producing aged debt and receivables reports, identifying errors and following them through.
- Documenting outstanding items and procedures for a clean handover at the end of the assignment.

What we are looking for

You will have hands-on experience in accounts receivable, sales ledger or credit control, including invoicing and cash allocation. Bank reconciliation and cashbook experience are essential, along with good Excel skills and a careful, organised approach. Exposure to VAT, sales tax, stock or inventory processes and Microsoft Dynamics would be useful.

title: Credit Controller
description:
As a Credit Controller in Reading, you will take ownership of a portfolio of customer accounts, ensuring payments are collected in line with agreed terms while building strong relationships with both customers and internal stakeholders. Working closely with the wider Finance team, you will manage debt recovery, resolve account queries, reconcile customer balances, and help support healthy cash flow across the business.

Client Details
- Established international organisation
- Operates in the retail industry
- Located in Reading

Description

Credit Controller responsibilities:
- Manage the full accounts receivable and credit control cycle for a portfolio of customer accounts, ensuring account records remain accurate, up to date, and compliant
- Chase outstanding debt through phone and email contact, negotiating payment plans where required and ensuring payments are received within agreed terms
- Act as the primary point of contact for customer account queries, resolving payment issues, disputes, invoice discrepancies, pricing queries and short payments in a timely manner
- Allocate and reconcile incoming receipts, maintaining accurate customer ledgers and investigating any unreconciled items
- Conduct credit checks and risk assessments for new and existing customers, monitoring credit exposure and recommending credit limit amendments, account holds or releases where appropriate
- Build strong relationships with customers, Sales, Customer Services and Finance teams to support effective issue resolution and minimise aged debt
- Maintain ownership of the aged debt ledger, monitoring overdue balances, analysing payment trends and identifying potential financial risks
- Support month-end activities by ensuring cash postings, reconciliations, credit notes, adjustments and promotional credits are processed accurately and within deadlines
- Identify opportunities to improve processes, strengthen controls and enhance the efficiency of the credit control and accounts receivable function
- Provide wider support to the Finance team, as required

Profile

A successful Credit Controller should have:
- Previous experience within Credit Control, Accounts Receivable or a similar finance function
- Proven track record of managing customer accounts and reducing overdue debt
- Microsoft Excel skills, including the use of Pivot Tables, VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP
- Experience using ERP or accounting systems such as SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, Sage or similar finance platforms
- Confident communicating with customers and internal stakeholders
- Highly organised with the ability to manage multiple priorities
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills

Job Offer

Credit Controller:
- Salary: £30,000 to £34,000 per annum - dependent on experience
- Competitive benefits package (TBC)
- Reading location, well-connected by public transport
- Hybrid working
- A supportive and inclusive workplace culture

title: Junior Finance & Operations Assistant
description:
Junior Finance & Business Operations Assistant

Location: Aldermaston, Berkshire UK Salary: 27,000

This Junior Finance & Business Operations Assistant role is ideal for someone looking to develop a long-term career in finance, with hands-on experience across sales ledger, purchase ledger, credit control, and wider business operations.

The successful candidate will be organised, hardworking, and detail-oriented, with a proactive approach and a willingness to learn. This role offers the opportunity to develop practical finance skills, gain exposure to business operations, and progress towards a more senior or management position over time.

Key Requirements
- A degree in Finance, Accounting, or a related subject would be advantageous.
- An AAT Level 2 qualification, or willingness to work towards one, would be beneficial.
- Strong English and Maths skills, ideally with GCSE grades of 6 or above.
- A hardworking, reliable attitude and a genuine willingness to learn.
- An interest in developing a long-term career in finance and business operations.
- Good communication skills and the ability to work effectively with colleagues, customers, and suppliers.

Career Development

This is an excellent opportunity for someone at the start of their career to gain practical experience across core finance functions, particularly sales and purchase ledger, credit control, and business operations. With training, experience, and continued development, there is potential to progress into a more senior finance position or management role in the future.
